title: Polenta Gnocchi with Fennel and Garlic Sauce
subtitle: baked polenta cubes with confit garlic and white wine
description: Creamy mascarpone polenta is set, cut into cubes and baked until golden, then served with roasted fennel, cherry tomatoes and confit garlic in a white wine sauce. Finished with lemon zest, hazelnuts and shaved parmesan.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Bring the milk, water and salt to the boil in a small pot. Gradually add the polenta, stirring constantly, until the mixture just reaches the boil.
Reduce the heat and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth. Remove from the heat and stir in the mascarpone.
Pour into the tray to a depth of about 1.5 cm and smooth the top. Sprinkle with half the parmesan and leave to set for about 1 hour at room temperature, or overnight in the fridge.
Cut the polenta into squares, place on the tray with gaps between and bake for about 7 minutes until golden. The cubes can be frozen before baking for up to 2 months.

Meanwhile, line another tray with baking paper and divide it with a foil barrier. Toss the thinly sliced fennel with olive oil, thyme leaves, salt and pepper and spread on one half. Bake for 10 minutes in the lower part of the oven.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes to the other half of the tray and roast for about 5 minutes more.

Heat a heavy frying pan, add the butter, garlic, oil from the garlic, chopped sage, fennel, roasted tomatoes and wine. Bring to the boil and cook for about 5 minutes until the wine has almost evaporated, stirring occasionally.
Place warm polenta cubes on plates, pour over the sauce, and top with lemon zest, chopped hazelnuts and shaved parmesan. Serve immediately.
